mathematical_audit.endpoint_chart: Item365's p-unit endpoint coefficient eliminates d1, leaving d2 and the retained loads as independent polynomial coordinates over F_p.
mathematical_audit.localization: On chart j, setting X_j=0 and inverting the outside loads does not change contraction because no inverted variable lies in the prime ideal (X_j). The chart kernel is exactly (X_j).
mathematical_audit.intersection: Distinct coordinate variables are pairwise coprime primes in the polynomial ring, so the intersection of all singleton-chart ideals is the principal product ideal (product_j X_j).
mathematical_audit.degree: A nonzero numerator in the product ideal contains every active load and has total load degree at least N. A lower-degree numerator or one omitting a load must be the zero polynomial modulo p.
mathematical_audit.content: An integer polynomial is zero modulo p exactly when p divides every coefficient, equivalently p divides its positive coefficient content. Hence a prime-independent low-degree generic residual captures actual singleton primes only through a nonzero content carrier.
mathematical_audit.portfolio: A noncontent numerator assigned chart set S must contain product_(j in S) X_j and pay degree at least |S|. A full noncontent cover pays total degree at least N; charts not so paid must enter content branches.
mathematical_audit.admission: Primitive content captures no prime, the zero polynomial is not a nonzero carrier, candidate-dependent constants merely insert the target primes, and a denominator vanishing on a chart is undefined.
mathematical_audit.scope: The theorem concerns generic localized chart identities. It does not close accidental correlations at the unique canonical point or full-support degree-N beta-height states. No actual sub-beta content is constructed.
